questions: Does the 5-sensor spread at ±0.03 m leave the signal saturated or dead-zoned at any offset, and at what lateral error?
Does the 0.04 m forward offset give enough lead on the tightest bends, or does the signal lag?
Is the 0.12 m wheel track giving enough turn authority without oscillation at the chosen base speed?
Does sensor noise at 12 mm footprints dominate the signal when the line is only partly under the outer sensors?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: Report which geometry field most limits the controller, if any.

intent: Establish a symmetric, five-sensor baseline with moderate spread (±0.03 m), 12 mm footprints, sensors 0.04 m ahead of the axle, and a light, compact body. The aim is a reliable platform that completes all three development tracks, from which later iterations can tune spread, forward offset, and sensor size against measured line error.
learning: Baseline entry: no prior evidence. Next iteration should adjust sensor spread, forward offset, or sensor size based on the first race's rms_error, max_error, and line_loss_events.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry or integration feedback yet, so this is a baseline built from the contract's constraints. Five sensors spread evenly across ±0.03 m give a steering signal that interpolates smoothly across the 25 mm tape, and 12 mm footprints keep each sensor sensitive to the line without losing it on small offsets. Sensors sit 0.04 m ahead of the axle so the controller gets advance warning of bends before the wheels reach them. The 0.12 m wheel track and 0.03 m wheel radius give moderate turn authority and a top speed that can meet the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in 3 s. Body width 0.12 m sets the off-track limit at max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03) = 0.06 m, which is the most forgiving the contract allows for the tape. Mass 0.7 kg keeps inertia low for quick response. I expect this to complete the development tracks with few line-loss events. The main uncertainty is whether 0.03 m sensor spread is too wide for tight slalom bends, which the Integrator's feedback should confirm.
